strongest_suspected_weakness: GitHubAuthorizationConsumerAdapter maps ConsumerOutcome values through string lookup dict _OUTCOME_TO_REFUSAL. If the Lane A authorization consumer adds a new outcome value not in the mapping, it defaults to 'authorization_revoked' which is fail-closed but may obscure the real refusal reason. Recovery: add new outcome to mapping dict when Lane A extends ConsumerOutcome.
proposed_reviewer_attack_surface: F1: Async context manager exception paths — exception during yield in branch_publication_lock tests that lock_fd is always closed in finally block

F2: Cross-process lock contention — fcntl advisory locks are process-local; separate Python processes on the same machine do not share locks; concurrent publication from different processes could bypass serialization
F3: Sha256 collision attacks on target_identity_digest — content digest is not a cryptographic binding; an attacker crafting a different owner/repo/branch with the same sha256 could replant evidence
F4: Evidence ledger append-only guarantee — fcntl advisory lock is not mandatory; a process ignoring the lock could corrupt the JSONL ledger

F5: AuthorizationConsumer protocol injection — if auth_consumer is set to a malicious adapter that claims authorized=True for all operations, authorization is bypassed; the protocol trusts the adapter
F6: build_publication_projection reads raw JSONL ledger outside lock — projection is a snapshot at read time; concurrent writes may produce incomplete projections
F7: operation_id uniqueness not enforced across instances — two services with same operation_id to different repos could produce evidence collisions if target_identity_digest not checked
F8: evidence_linkage fields populated before ledger write — if terminal_receipt_digest is computed before the receipt is written, it could reference a receipt that fails to write
F9: No remote publication truth — all evidence is local; no remote main verification of published claims
